inputs.label: Children with diarrhoea who receive ORS
inputs.meaning: Of children under five who had diarrhoea in the last two weeks, the share who were given ORS. The lower this is, the more children the campaign can help.
inputs.where: The latest DHS or MICS survey for the location. National figures are in UNICEF's data warehouse.
inputs.range: 10% (Mali, 2024 survey) to 85% (Sierra Leone, 2019 survey), median 36% (45 sub-Saharan countries, latest survey in each, 2006 to 2025)

inputs.label: Under-five diarrhoea deaths per 100,000 children, per year
inputs.meaning: How many children under five die of diarrhoea each year, per 100,000 children. This matters more than any other input. If it doubles, the result roughly doubles.
inputs.where: UN IGME (childmortality.org), IHME Global Burden of Disease, or WHO Global Health Estimates. They can disagree by up to three times for the same location, so note which one you used. The example locations use UN IGME's 2024 under-five diarrhoea deaths (its CA CODE cause-of-death estimates), divided by UN WPP 2024 population.
inputs.range: 10 (Sao Tome and Principe) to 328 (Nigeria), median 97 (45 sub-Saharan countries, UN IGME / CA CODE 2024 diarrhoea deaths, UN WPP 2024 population)

inputs.label: Scaling factor applied to the death rate
inputs.meaning: Puts a death rate on another source's level, for example to bring an older study in line with a newer national estimate. 1 leaves the rate as entered.
inputs.where: Divide one source's national figure by the other's. For example, use 0.5 if the newer national figure is half the study's.

inputs.label: Children already receiving vitamin A supplements
inputs.meaning: Share of children aged 6 to 59 months who had a vitamin A dose in the last six months. Children who already had one gain nothing from another.
inputs.where: The latest DHS or MICS survey for the location.
inputs.range: 20% (Gabon, 2021 survey) to 84% (Namibia, 2013 survey), median 56% (37 countries with a survey figure, latest survey in each, 2007 to 2025)

inputs.label: Child death rate, ages 6 to 59 months, per year
inputs.meaning: Share of children aged 6 to 59 months who die each year, from any cause. The vitamin A benefit goes up with it.
inputs.where: Work it out from UN IGME under-five and infant mortality (childmortality.org) with this formula, which gives a yearly rate for ages one to four: 1 - (1 - (U5MR - IMR) / (1000 - IMR)) ^ (1/4). Child mortality from a DHS survey also works. The model applies this ages one to four rate to children aged 6 to 59 months; the difference is small.
inputs.range: 0.0003 (Botswana) to 0.0126 (Nigeria), median 0.0041 (45 sub-Saharan countries, UN IGME 2024)

inputs.label: Rotavirus vaccine coverage gained since the death rate's year
inputs.meaning: How much rotavirus vaccine coverage has gone up since the year of the death rate. The vaccine now prevents some of those deaths, so the model takes them out.
inputs.where: WHO and UNICEF immunisation estimates (WUENIC). Take coverage now minus coverage in the year of the death rate. Enter 0 if the death rate is recent. If the vaccine was introduced after that year, enter today's full coverage.
inputs.range: 0 for most countries with 2024 death rates. Higher where the vaccine is new, for example introduced in 2025

inputs.label: Apply the rotavirus adjustment (1 = yes, 0 = no)
inputs.meaning: Whether to take out deaths that rotavirus vaccine has prevented since the year of the death rate (see the location inputs above).
inputs.where: GiveWell's CHAI Bauchi model uses it.

inputs.label: Children aged 12 to 59 months dewormed in the last six months
inputs.meaning: Share of young children who were given deworming medicine in the six months before the survey. Children already dewormed gain nothing from another dose, so the campaign's deworming benefit falls as this rises.
inputs.where: The latest DHS or MICS survey for the location: deworming medication in the past six months (the DHS online database reports it for children 6 to 59 months). The 46% here is the median of 36 sub-Saharan countries with a DHS figure. This counts children not dewormed recently; some of them would be reached anyway, for example by child health weeks. GiveWell treats the true share Connect adds as unknown (it guessed 15% to 40% in its Connect pilot spreadsheet) and expects a trial to measure it.
inputs.range: 13% (Ethiopia, 2016 survey) to 82% (Rwanda, 2019-20 survey), median 46% (36 countries with a DHS figure, latest survey in each, 2006 to 2021; many surveys are old)

inputs.label: Worm burden, as a share of the level in the Kenya trial
inputs.meaning: How heavy worm infections are in the location compared with Busia, Kenya, in 1998, where the trial behind the income evidence was run. The income benefit is scaled by this share.
inputs.where: GiveWell's deworming cost-effectiveness spreadsheets give a figure for each area its grantees work in (for example row 42 of its Deworm the World analysis). The 9.3% here is the median of the 19 sub-Saharan countries in GiveWell's END Fund, SCI and Sightsavers spreadsheets. Each country's figure is in GiveWell's January 2022 SCI grant spreadsheet (see Sources).
inputs.range: 0.9% (Uganda) to 21% (Kenya, Madagascar, Mauritania), median 9.3% (19 sub-Saharan countries in GiveWell's deworming spreadsheets, January 2022)

inputs.label: Cost per child reached, per visit, for ORS and vitamin A
inputs.meaning: Everything the organisation spends per child per visit for ORS and zinc and the vitamin A capsule, including commodities, local partner costs and the Connect platform fee. The deworming tablet is added separately. Halve the cost and the result doubles.
inputs.where: The program budget. $1.80 is Connect's September 2026 estimate. Low is $2.50. High is $1.44, 20% below $1.80.

inputs.label: Campaigns per year
inputs.meaning: How many door-to-door rounds a year. A second round doubles the cost, adds 0.8 of a round's ORS benefit (see Value of a second round, under Judgement calls) and gives a second vitamin A dose. The deworming tablet is given again in the second round but counts as the same year of deworming, so it adds its cost and no benefit.
inputs.where: The program design.

inputs.label: Vitamin A included (1 = yes, 0 = no)
inputs.meaning: Whether the visit also gives children aged 6 months and over a vitamin A dose. At 0 the vitamin A deaths prevented and the capsule cost are zero, so the result is for the visit without vitamin A. The cost per visit for ORS stays the same.
inputs.where: The program design.

inputs.label: Extra cost of the vitamin A capsule, per child per visit
inputs.meaning: Any vitamin A cost not already in the cost per visit.
inputs.where: The program budget. Enter 0 while the capsule is in the cost per visit.

inputs.label: Deworming included (1 = yes, 0 = no)
inputs.meaning: Whether the visit also gives children aged 12 months and over a deworming tablet. At 0 the deworming value and the tablet cost are zero, so the result is for the visit without deworming.
inputs.where: The program design. Child health campaigns usually give deworming with vitamin A, from 12 months of age.

inputs.label: Extra cost of the deworming tablet, per child per visit
inputs.meaning: Any deworming cost not already in the cost per visit. Albendazole 400 mg chewable tablets cost about $0.04 each at UNICEF's indicative price. Where the Ministry of Health supplies donated tablets, enter 0.
inputs.where: UNICEF Supply Catalogue, albendazole 400 mg chewable tablets, $3.66 per 100 (accessed October 13, 2026).

inputs.label: Delivery model (1 = door to door, 2 = free pickup)
inputs.meaning: Bringing ORS to the home raises ORS use more than free ORS that families have to collect. Connect campaigns are door to door.
inputs.where: Wagner et al. 2019 trial, as GiveWell uses it. Door to door is 0.469 (GiveWell's CHAI Bauchi model). Free pickup is 0.399 (GiveWell's general model).

inputs.label: Share of the year's diarrhoea episodes the co-packs cover
inputs.meaning: Whether families have ORS and zinc for every bout of diarrhoea in the year. GiveWell assumes they do, and its cost per child pays for a treatment course for every bout: about 1.8 a year for children under five. A Connect visit leaves two co-packs per child, which roughly matches. One co-pack with no restock would cover about half a child's bouts (0.55).
inputs.where: GiveWell's ORS and zinc spreadsheet: bouts a year from IHME, 2.5 for infants and 1.7 for ages 1 to 4. Two co-packs per child: Connect's program design.

inputs.label: Vitamin A dose: reduction in child deaths
inputs.meaning: How much one vitamin A dose lowers a child's risk of dying from any cause over the following six months.
inputs.where: GiveWell's vitamin A report, April 2026 update, gives 1% to 11%. 6% is our midpoint of that range, not a GiveWell figure: GiveWell works out a figure for each location it models (1.3% to 11.1% across 33 locations in its Helen Keller spreadsheet, median 2.9%). Low is 1%, High is 11%.

inputs.label: Value of a second round, as a share of the first (ORS)
inputs.meaning: Most of the rise in ORS use, about 80%, happens in the first six months after a distribution. So a second round six months later counts as 0.8 of the first. No study has measured this directly.
inputs.where: Our assumption. Only used when there are 2 campaigns a year. Low is 0.5, High is 1.

inputs.label: Share of the vitamin A benefit that works through diarrhoea
inputs.meaning: A child saved by the vitamin A dose may also have been saved by ORS. This share stops the model counting those children twice. Apart from this, the model treats the two as separate. At the typical location the model removes about 11% of the vitamin A deaths as overlap; if all of the vitamin A benefit worked through diarrhoea it would remove about 28%.
inputs.where: Our assumption, as there is no published figure. Diarrhoea causes only a small share of child deaths, so 0.4 is on the cautious side. At 0, the result goes up by about 2%. Low is 1 and High is 0: the higher the share, the more of the vitamin A benefit is removed as overlap with ORS.

inputs.label: Adjustment for deworming children aged 1 to 4 rather than school age
inputs.meaning: The income evidence comes from children aged about 7 to 14 at treatment. Follow-ups found that children under five at the time also gained, in learning scores years later; no study has measured their adult income. 1 treats a year of deworming at ages 1 to 4 as worth the same as a year at school age; 0.5 as half.
inputs.where: GiveWell's June 2024 cost-effectiveness spreadsheet for the Connect pilot in Nigeria uses the full school-age value for children 6 to 59 months, the same as 1. Ozier 2018 (children under two during the Kenya program; cognitive gains ten years later) and Croke 2014 (Uganda, ages 1 to 7; literacy and numeracy gains seven to eight years later) support an effect; neither gives a factor. Low is 0.5, High is 1.

inputs.label: Years until the income benefit starts, deworming
inputs.meaning: How long after deworming the higher earnings begin. A child dewormed at ages 1 to 4 starts work later than the school-age children in the trial, so the income gain is discounted for a longer wait.
inputs.where: GiveWell's deworming parameter note: treated children average 9 years old and start substantive work at about 17, giving its 8 years. Connect deworms children aged 1 to 4 (about 3 on average), so the same reasoning gives about 14; we use 15, GiveWell's figure for lead exposure, which starts at birth (Pure Earth grant spreadsheet, row 58). GiveWell's June 2024 Connect pilot spreadsheet took Deworm the World's school-age value (an 8-year wait) without adjusting for age. Low is 17 years (work from age 20), High is 11 (work from 14, the youngest legal working age GiveWell's note cites).

inputs.label: Funging adjustment
inputs.meaning: Discount for the chance that others would have funded the program anyway.
inputs.where: GiveWell's CHAI Bauchi grant page (September 2023), the same grant as the government share and door to door delivery. GiveWell's general ORS and zinc model uses 0.968 for its low-income case.

inputs.label: GiveWell benchmark, units of value per dollar
inputs.meaning: Every result is divided by this. The funding bar is 6 times this figure (May 2026).
inputs.where: GiveWell's cost-effectiveness page, September 2026. Its 2023 ORS analysis used 0.00335, which makes results about 10% lower.

inputs.label: Government cost, as a share of the organisation's cost
inputs.meaning: What the government spends on the campaign, in cash or in kind, for every dollar the organisation spends. GiveWell takes off the good that money could have done elsewhere (its leveraging adjustment). At 0% there is nothing to take off, so the adjustment is 1 (Model tab, Step 8).
inputs.where: 0%: in Connect campaigns the organisation pays for the work and the government gives permission, as in GiveWell's CHAI Bauchi ORS and zinc grant. GiveWell's general ORS and zinc model guesses 100% for government-run programs (the grey columns on the Model tab). The model covers a 0% share only, so this cell accepts only 0.

inputs.label: Trial effect of ORS brought to the home
inputs.type: Study: Wagner et al. 2019, via GiveWell's CHAI Bauchi model
inputs.meaning: Of children who would not otherwise have had ORS, the share who get it when it is brought free to the home.
inputs.where: Wagner et al. 2019 (Uganda), door-to-door group, as used in GiveWell's CHAI Bauchi model.

inputs.label: Trial effect of free ORS that families collect
inputs.type: Study: Wagner et al. 2019, via GiveWell's ORS and zinc model
inputs.meaning: The same, when families have to collect the free ORS themselves.
inputs.where: Wagner et al. 2019, free pickup group, as used in GiveWell's general ORS model.

inputs.label: Discount for the trial's own weaknesses
inputs.meaning: The trial relied on what families reported and was not blinded, so 80% of its effect is counted.
inputs.where: GiveWell ORS and zinc analysis, August 2023.

inputs.label: Discount for using the trial elsewhere
inputs.meaning: The trial was at one site near a city and followed families for a short time, so 85% of the effect is counted elsewhere.
inputs.where: GiveWell ORS and zinc analysis, August 2023.

inputs.label: Extra deaths where diarrhoea contributed
inputs.meaning: For every death caused by diarrhoea, half as many again where diarrhoea contributed but was not the main cause.
inputs.where: GiveWell ORS and zinc analysis, August 2023.

inputs.label: Reduction in diarrhoea deaths for a child who uses ORS
inputs.meaning: The original studies found 93% fewer deaths. This is discounted twice, by 0.8 each time.
inputs.where: GiveWell ORS and zinc analysis, August 2023 (93% x 0.8 x 0.8).

inputs.label: Share of diarrhoea deaths caused by rotavirus
inputs.meaning: Used only by the rotavirus adjustment.
inputs.where: GBD 2021 Diarrhoeal Diseases Collaborators, Lancet Infectious Diseases 2024.

inputs.label: Rotavirus vaccine efficacy against death
inputs.meaning: Used only by the rotavirus adjustment.
inputs.where: GiveWell CHAI Bauchi model.

inputs.label: Country adjustment to vaccine efficacy
inputs.meaning: Used only by the rotavirus adjustment.
inputs.where: GiveWell CHAI Bauchi model.

inputs.label: Share of children reached who are 6 to 59 months old
inputs.meaning: Vitamin A is given from six months of age, so it covers 54 of the 60 months before a child turns five.
inputs.where: 54 divided by 60.

inputs.label: Protection from one vitamin A dose
inputs.meaning: One dose protects for about six months, so one campaign a year covers half the year.
inputs.where: GiveWell vitamin A report.

inputs.label: Value of preventing one child's death
inputs.meaning: Value given to preventing the death of a child under five, in units of value.
inputs.where: Rounded from GiveWell's ORS and zinc model, which uses 111.8 to 112.7 depending on the place. GiveWell's 2025 moral weights give 116.25 for a death under five from malaria and 118.73 for vitamin A.

inputs.label: Share of the benefit that comes from deaths prevented
inputs.meaning: The other 10% comes from illness avoided and better development. The model adds it by dividing by 0.9.
inputs.where: GiveWell ORS and zinc analysis, August 2023.

inputs.label: Adjustment for effects not modelled
inputs.meaning: A small increase for benefits the model does not count, such as zinc making illness shorter.
inputs.where: GiveWell ORS and zinc analysis, August 2023.

inputs.label: Share of children reached who are 12 to 59 months old
inputs.meaning: Deworming is given from 12 months of age, so it covers 48 of the 60 months before a child turns five.
inputs.where: 48 divided by 60, as for vitamin A.

inputs.label: Effect of deworming on ln income in the Kenya trial, intention to treat
inputs.meaning: The gain in adult income, in natural log units, for children assigned to the trial's treatment group, pooled across the follow-up surveys; about 11.5%.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 7 (the Kenya Life Panel Survey follow-ups of Miguel and Kremer 2004).

inputs.label: Coverage in the trial's treatment group
inputs.meaning: Not every child assigned to treatment was dewormed, and a few control children were. The effect on those assigned is converted into the effect on those treated.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 8.

inputs.label: Coverage in the trial's control group
inputs.meaning: See the row above.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 9.

inputs.label: Replicability adjustment for the income effect
inputs.meaning: Counts 13% of the trial's income effect: one trial, a long chain from infection to adult income, and heavier infections then than now make the full effect unlikely to repeat.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 11.

inputs.label: Adjustment for the trial's treatment schedule against a program year
inputs.meaning: Takes 10% off because a year of treatment in the trial was heavier than a year of treatment in today's programs.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 12.

inputs.label: Extra years of deworming in the trial's treatment group
inputs.meaning: The treatment group received this many more years of deworming than the control group, so the gain per year of deworming is the trial effect divided by this.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 13 (Baird et al. 2016).

inputs.label: Adjustment for the effect fading over time
inputs.meaning: The later follow-ups found smaller effects than the earlier ones, so 10% comes off the present value.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 22; explained in its April 2023 update on deworming and decay.

inputs.label: Multiplier for resource sharing within households, deworming
inputs.meaning: Doubles the value of an income gain because income is shared within the household.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 25.

inputs.label: Years the income benefit lasts
inputs.meaning: The gain is counted over 40 working years, as an annuity due.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, rows 19 and 21.

inputs.label: Discount rate
inputs.meaning: Future income is discounted at 4% a year.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 16.

inputs.label: Units of value per unit of ln income, for one person for one year
inputs.meaning: One unit of value is doubling one person's consumption for a year, which is 0.69 in natural log units, so one log unit is worth 1.44 units.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, row 44; 1 divided by ln(2).

inputs.label: Adjustment for effects not modelled, deworming
inputs.meaning: Net addition for effects outside the income chain: direct health effects, HIV reduction, deaths averted, short-term anaemia, investment of the income gain and other long-run benefits, less possible harms, drug resistance, unprogrammed deworming, lower-priority areas and general equilibrium effects. The organisation-level adjustments (wastage, monitoring, fungibility) are not carried, as the ORS chain carries none.
inputs.where: GiveWell, Deworm the World 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis, rows 96 to 110.

rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: The effect on the treated, times the replicability and schedule adjustments, divided by the extra years of deworming: 0.0076, GiveWell's row 14. A year of deworming is that year's full schedule, so a second campaign in the year does not double it.

rows.label: Worm burden, as a share of the level in the Kenya trial
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: From the Inputs tab, or the Scenarios tab (GiveWell's figures for the area).

rows.label: Adjustment for ages 1 to 4 rather than school age
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: From the Inputs tab. Our assumption, the main judgement call for deworming: 1 assumes a child dewormed at ages 1 to 4 gains as much in adult income as a school-age child. No study has measured it. The Sensitivity tab shows 0.5.

rows.label: Effect on ln income per child dewormed for one year, in this location
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming

rows.label: Years until the income benefit starts
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: From the Inputs tab. 15: a child dewormed at ages 1 to 4 starts work later than the school-age children behind GiveWell's 8 years (row 17). The Sensitivity tab shows 17 and 11.

rows.label: Years the income benefit lasts
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab (40 years).

rows.label: Discount rate
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab (4%).

rows.label: Value today of one log unit a year over the benefit years, if it started now
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: GiveWell's present value with payments at the start of each year (row 21): 20.58 for 40 years at 4%.

rows.label: Discount for the years until the benefit starts
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: The discount rate applied once for each year of waiting (row 18).

rows.label: Present value of one log unit a year over the benefit years, discounted for the wait
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: The two rows above multiplied. At an 8-year wait this is 15.04.

rows.label: Adjustment for the effect fading over time
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: A 10% reduction (row 22). Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab.

rows.label: Multiplier for resource sharing within households
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: GiveWell's 2.0 (row 25). Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab.

rows.label: Income gain per child dewormed for one year, present value (ln units)
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: At a worm burden of 100%, an age adjustment of 1 and an 8-year wait this reproduces GiveWell's 0.206 per year of deworming (row 27).

rows.label: Units of value per unit of ln income
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab (GiveWell row 44; 1 divided by ln 2).

rows.label: Adjustment for effects not modelled, deworming
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: GiveWell's 1.073 for effects outside the income chain (rows 96 to 110). Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab.

rows.label: Units of value from deworming per 100,000 children reached, per year
rows.step: Step 6. Income gains from deworming
rows.note: Children reached, times the share old enough, times the share not already dewormed, times the value of each child's income gain. Zero when deworming is switched off.

rows.label: Extra cost of the vitamin A capsule, per child per visit
rows.step: Step 7. ORS and zinc + vitamin A together, and the full package
rows.note: From the Inputs tab; zero when vitamin A is switched off. The cost per visit for ORS stays the same either way.

rows.label: Deaths prevented per 100,000 children, both together
rows.step: Step 7. ORS and zinc + vitamin A together, and the full package

rows.label: Cost per child per year, both together
rows.step: Step 7. ORS and zinc + vitamin A together, and the full package

rows.label: Extra cost of the deworming tablet, per child per visit
rows.step: Step 7. ORS and zinc + vitamin A together, and the full package
rows.note: From the Inputs tab; zero when deworming is switched off.

rows.label: Cost per child per year, full package
rows.step: Step 7. ORS and zinc + vitamin A together, and the full package
rows.note: The ORS and zinc + vitamin A cost plus the tablet for every campaign in the year.

rows.label: Value of preventing one child's death (units)
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value
rows.note: Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab. The grey columns use GiveWell's age-weighted values for each case.

rows.label: Share of the benefit from deaths prevented
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value
rows.note: The rest is illness avoided and effects on development. Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab. The grey columns use GiveWell's own shares.

rows.label: Adjustment for effects not modelled
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value
rows.note: Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab.

rows.label: Value per death prevented, before leveraging and funging (units)
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value

rows.label: Government cost, as a share of the organisation's cost
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value
rows.note: Fixed assumption on the Inputs tab. 0%: in Connect campaigns the organisation pays for the work and the government gives permission, as in GiveWell's CHAI Bauchi grant. GiveWell's general ORS and zinc cases (the grey columns) assume 100%.

rows.label: Adjustment for government spending (GiveWell's leveraging adjustment)
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value
rows.note: GiveWell takes off the good the government's money would have done elsewhere. With a 0% government share there is nothing to take off, so this is 1. The model covers a 0% government share only. The grey columns use GiveWell's own values for its cases (0.797 and 0.886).

rows.label: Units of value per 100,000 children per year, before leveraging and funging
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value
rows.note: Deaths prevented by ORS and zinc + vitamin A, times the value of each, plus the deworming units.

rows.label: Value per dollar before leveraging and funging (units)
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value
rows.note: Units of value per year divided by the cost per year. The grey columns: ORS and zinc only (deaths prevented times the value of each, divided by the ORS cost).

rows.label: Funging adjustment
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value
rows.note: From the Inputs tab. The grey columns use GiveWell's own values for each case.

rows.label: GiveWell benchmark, units of value per dollar
rows.step: Step 8. Value of each death prevented, and of the package, in units of value
rows.note: From the Inputs tab. The grey columns use 0.00335, the figure in GiveWell's August 2023 analysis.

rows.label: Cost-effectiveness: multiple of GiveWell's benchmark
rows.step: Step 9. Result
rows.note: Value per dollar, times the leveraging and funging adjustments, divided by the benchmark, for the package switched on in the Inputs tab. Quote this one figure: splitting it between ORS, vitamin A and deworming would depend on how the visit cost is divided. The grey columns give 6.12x and 12.22x, the results on the Simple CEA tab of GiveWell's ORS and zinc spreadsheet.
